name: System Paluda
summary: A complete paludarium in a box: glass tank, a black wabi-kusa wall with a small pump that keeps it wet, a Mistflow fogger and a circulation fan. You add the plants, a light and water. It takes most of the guesswork out of building a planted wall that stays damp.
highlights: Two footprints: 30 x 30 cm or 60 x 30 cm, both 45 cm tall
Includes a 3 L/min USB circulation pump that trickles water down the wabi-kusa wall
Mistflow fogger and Circulation Fan 40 come in the box
Wall is built from wabi-kusa mats (9 on the 30, 18 on the 60) you plant straight into
Sliding glass top, top plate and a stainless mesh cover for adjusting humidity
bestFor: Someone who wants a mossy, misty rainforest wall or a jewel orchid display without designing the plumbing and airflow from scratch.
watchOut: No light is included, so budget for a Paluda Light II or similar, and the USB adapter is missing from the C-plug version.

specs.Included: Tank, Mistflow box and Mistflow, wabi-kusa mats, circulation pump, pump stand, outflow pipe, Circulation Fan 40, sliding glass top, top glass plate, stainless mesh cover, drainage piece, sponges, Paluda Clean PC, cascade brush
specs.Plug options: With USB power adapter, or C-plug version without the adapter

name: Neo Glass Paluda
summary: The glass box from the System Paluda sold on its own, with the sliding top and top plate but none of the wall, pump or fogger. It suits people who want to design their own layout, or who already own misting and fan gear.
highlights: Same 30 x 30 x 45 cm and 60 x 30 x 45 cm sizes as the System Paluda
Sliding glass top and fixed top plate included
Drainage piece and one 40 mm hole cap for adding a fan or plumbing
Accepts DOOA's Circulation Fan 40 and Spray Pump as add-ons
bestFor: Keepers building a custom paludarium or terrarium layout who want a tidy, rimless-looking glass enclosure made for the job.
watchOut: It is only the enclosure, so you still need a light, a misting or watering method and airflow.

specs.Included: Tank, sliding glass top, top glass plate, 40 mm hole cap, drainage piece

name: Glass Paluda
summary: A tall all-glass display piece: a 60 x 30 x 40 cm case sits on top of a glass frame with two glass shelves underneath, the whole thing standing a metre high. It is designed for hanging epiphytes, air plants and mounted wood rather than a water feature.
highlights: Overall 60 x 40 x 100 cm, display case 60 x 30 x 40 cm
Glass lid plus hooks for hanging mounted plants or wood inside
Two glass shelves below for pots or equipment
Maximum load capacity of 10 kg
bestFor: Showing off mounted epiphytes, orchids or a driftwood branch as furniture in a room, where a normal tank on a cabinet would feel too heavy.
watchOut: The 10 kg load limit means it suits light mounted displays, not heavy soil and stone builds.

specs.Included: Glass lid, two lid pads, two Glass Paluda hooks, non-slip stickers, high-absorption sponge

name: Neo Glass Air
summary: Small open-top glass cubes and columns for terrariums, moss towers and wabi-kusa displays. There are eight sizes, from a 9 cm tall tray to a 45 cm tall column, so it is easy to match one to a desk, shelf or light stand.
highlights: Eight sizes from 15 x 15 x 25 cm up to 30 x 30 x 45 cm
Low trays (9 and 12 cm tall) for wabi-kusa balls or moss landscapes
Tall columns pair with DOOA's Terra Base moss pillars
Frameless clear glass
bestFor: Desk or shelf terrariums, moss towers and small emersed plant displays where you want a clean glass box in an exact size.
watchOut: These are open boxes; a lid is sold separately (Neo Glass Cover), and without one humidity-loving plants will dry out quickly.

name: Neo Glass Terra H36
summary: A 60 cm glass tank with a stepped profile: 16 cm tall at the front and 36 cm at the back. The low front makes planting and trimming easy, while the tall back wall gives room for an emersed or mist-wall section above the waterline.
highlights: 60 x 30 cm footprint, 16 cm front height, 36 cm back height
Built for aquaterrarium layouts with water in front and plants climbing the back
Pairs with DOOA's Mizukusa Mist Wall and Wabi-Kusa Wall 60
Frameless glass that sits happily on a standard 60 cm stand
bestFor: Riparium and aquaterrarium builds on a 60 cm stand, where you want shallow water, emersed plants and a planted back wall in one tank.
watchOut: With only 16 cm at the front, water depth is shallow, so it is not a swap for a normal 60 cm fish tank.

name: Mizukusa Mist Wall
summary: A planted wall system that sits above the water of a normal aquarium. A small filter pumps tank water up to the top of a black wabi-kusa panel, which stays wet so you can grow emersed plants and moss above a submerged layout.
highlights: 600 fits inside ADA Cube Garden 60 cm tanks (25, 36 or 45 cm tall, or 60 x 45 x 36 cm)
900 and 1200 sit behind 90 cm and 120 cm Cube Gardens
Driven by an ADA Super Jet filter (ES-150 for the 600, ES-600 for the 900, ES-1200 for the 1200)
Comes with inflow and outflow pipes, suction clips and 12, 27 or 48 wabi-kusa mats
bestFor: Keepers who want an aquarium and an emersed planted wall in the same display, and already run or plan to run ADA filtration.
watchOut: The 900 and 1200 are made to order with roughly a two month wait, and each size is tied to a specific ADA filter and tank.

specs.Lead time: 900 and 1200 are made to order (about 2 months)

name: Terra Base
summary: A porous, dark clay-look pillar that wicks water upwards, so moss and small epiphytes can grow all over it. Stood in a tall Neo Glass Air with a little water in the base, it becomes a living moss tower.
highlights: Two heights: 16 cm and 23 cm, both 10 cm across
Sized for the Neo Glass Air 20 x 20 x 30 cm and 20 x 20 x 35 cm
Wicks water up from the base to keep moss damp
Takes moss, small ferns and miniature epiphytes
bestFor: A low-effort moss tower on a desk or shelf, especially if you already like the look of wabi-kusa.
watchOut: It needs a humid enclosure and regular top-ups; in open room air the top dries out and moss browns.

extra.Matching tank: Neo Glass Air 20 x 20 x 30 cm
Neo Glass Air 20 x 20 x 35 cm

name: Glass Pot Maru
summary: A round, handmade glass jar with a lid, made for small closed plantings like jewel orchids, moss and mini ferns. The lid holds humidity in, so it works well as a tabletop terrarium.
highlights: Two sizes: 9.5 cm across by 14.6 cm tall, and 13 cm by 20 cm
Lidded, so humidity stays high with little misting
Handmade glass, so exact sizes vary a little
bestFor: A first closed terrarium or a small moss display on a desk, with no equipment needed beyond some light.
watchOut: Small volume means condensation and mould can build up if it sits in direct sun or never gets aired.

name: Glass Pot Shizuku
summary: A handmade teardrop-shaped glass pot with a small lid, meant for a closed planting of moss, jewel orchids or small ferns. The narrow opening keeps humidity up and the shape looks good from any side.
highlights: Up to 17 cm across and 20 cm tall
Small 10.3 cm lid keeps moisture in
Matches DOOA's Wood Base Shizuku and Magnet Light G Slim for a lit display
bestFor: A single decorative terrarium piece on a desk or shelf, especially with a small clip-on or magnet light above it.
watchOut: The narrow neck makes planting and trimming fiddly, so long tweezers help.

specs.Lid: Up to 10.3 cm diameter, 2 cm tall

name: Cell
summary: A tall glass cloche that sits over a coloured glass dish, making a small closed terrarium for a single plant or a clump of moss. Lifting the dome off gives full access for planting and trimming.
highlights: 17 cm across and 30 cm tall
Removable glass dome over a planting dish
Base comes in green, amber or clear glass
Handmade, so sizes vary slightly
bestFor: Showing off one special plant (a jewel orchid, begonia or small aroid) as a decorative piece.
watchOut: It holds only a thin layer of substrate, so pick slow, compact plants.

name: Mistflow
summary: A small ultrasonic fogger that sits in water and sends a low layer of mist rolling across a paludarium or terrarium. It is mostly about raising humidity and giving that cloud-forest look.
highlights: Ultrasonic fogger that works submerged in shallow water
Included with the System Paluda, also sold on its own
Used in DOOA's Mizukusa Mist Wall and System Terra layouts
bestFor: Adding visible mist and a humidity boost to a paludarium or wabi-kusa display.
watchOut: Fog does not wet leaves as much as a spray system, and hard water leaves white scale on the disc and glass, so softened water helps.

name: Spray Pump
summary: A high-pressure misting pump with a plumbing kit for up to four spray points and six nozzles. Run on a timer, it gives plants in a paludarium a proper fine-mist watering rather than just fog.
highlights: Up to 70 psi for a fine, even mist
About 0.85 L per minute, so short timed bursts are enough
Up to four spray points and six nozzles, single and double heads included
Fits the Paludarium series and can go in a Neo Glass Paluda with an optional suction cup
bestFor: Larger paludariums and aquaterrariums with a lot of land planting that need regular, reliable misting.
watchOut: It needs its own water container, and tap water will spot the glass with calcium unless you soften it.

specs.Included: Single and double spray nozzles, T and L joints, pressure-resistant tube

name: Circulation Fan 40
summary: A compact 40 mm USB fan that mounts in the hole on DOOA's Paluda tanks and keeps air moving inside. Gentle airflow stops stagnant, mouldy corners and helps leaves dry between mistings.
highlights: Fits the 40 mm port on System Paluda and Neo Glass Paluda 30 and 60
USB powered (5 V, 1 A) with an inline controller
Included with the System Paluda
bestFor: Anyone running a closed Paluda enclosure who is fighting condensation, mould or rot.
watchOut: It only works with DOOA's Paluda tanks and does not come with a USB adapter.

name: Paluda Light II
summary: A slim, dark LED bar that sits on top of DOOA's Paluda enclosures. It gives strong light close up for the moss and small plants growing on a paludarium wall, with a very cool, bright white tone.
highlights: Two lengths with 21 or 50 LEDs
Around 15,000 lux at 10 cm
12 W and 25 W power draw
Rated for over 30,000 hours
bestFor: Lighting a System Paluda or Neo Glass Paluda where plants grow close to the light.
watchOut: The quoted colour temperature is very cool (around 19,000 to 23,000 K), so the look is bluish white rather than warm.

name: Magnet Light G Slim
summary: A small, flat round LED that attaches by magnet to DOOA's stands and arms. It is made for lighting glass pots, cloches and small terrariums from just above.
highlights: Compact disc light for small glass pots and terrariums
Magnetic mount for DOOA light stands and the mounting arm
Pairs with the Glass Pot Shizuku and Wood Base Shizuku as a set
bestFor: A single glass pot or small terrarium on a desk that needs its own neat light.
watchOut: It needs a DOOA stand or arm to hang from, sold separately.

name: Scissors Curve
summary: Curved-blade stainless scissors for trimming carpets, moss and stems. The curve lets you cut flat along the substrate without your hand blocking the view.
highlights: Two lengths: 17 cm and 23 cm
Curved blades for carpet and moss trimming
Stainless steel
bestFor: Trimming foreground carpets and moss in small to medium tanks and paludariums.
watchOut: The 17 cm version is short for tanks deeper than about 30 cm.

name: Scissors 105
summary: Short straight scissors for close, fiddly work in glass pots, terrariums and on wabi-kusa balls. Small enough to snip single leaves precisely.
highlights: Short straight blades for precise snips
Handy for wabi-kusa, glass pots and emersed plants
Stainless steel
bestFor: Trimming wabi-kusa and small terrarium plantings where long aquarium scissors are awkward.
watchOut: Too short to reach the bottom of a normal aquarium.

name: Tweezers
summary: Straight stainless planting tweezers in three lengths. Use them to push stems and small plants into soil and to place moss or small stones.
highlights: Three lengths: 17.5, 25.5 and 30 cm
Fine straight tips for planting stems and carpet portions
Stainless steel
bestFor: General planting in terrariums, paludariums and aquariums, picking the length to suit tank depth.

name: Tweezers Curve
summary: Stainless tweezers with an angled tip, which make it easier to plant at the back of a layout or behind hardscape without your hand getting in the way.
highlights: Bent tip for planting behind stones and wood
Two lengths
Stainless steel
bestFor: Planting and tidying in tight spots in terrariums, glass pots and busy aquascapes.

name: Soil Scraper 13
summary: A slim stainless spatula for moving and smoothing soil in glass pots, terrariums and small tanks. The narrow blade gets into tight gaps between stones and roots.
highlights: Narrow flat blade for smoothing and shaping soil
Useful in glass pots where a trowel will not fit
Stainless steel
bestFor: Terrarium and nano-tank builders who need to shape substrate in cramped spaces.

name: Aquasky RGB II
summary: ADA's slim RGB LED that stands on legs outside the glass of a 60 cm tank. It is controlled over Bluetooth from ADA's phone app, with colour, brightness and timer settings, and a soft fade on and off.
highlights: 70 RGB LEDs, up to 40,000 lux at 10 cm
Draws up to 66 W at full output
Legs rest outside the glass, so any glass thickness works on a 60 cm wide tank
Bluetooth app control with presets, colour tuning and a timer
Flicker-free, which helps when filming or photographing the tank
bestFor: A 60 cm planted tank where you want strong, tunable light and a clean ADA look without a separate controller.
watchOut: It is made for 60 cm tanks only, and full power is a lot of light for a low-tech tank without CO2.

specs.Colour temperature: About 8,000 to 11,000 K in default mode

name: Pollen Glass Beetle
summary: ADA's glass CO2 diffuser with a flat ceramic disc held between two suction cups. The number is the disc diameter, so bigger discs push out more fine bubbles for larger tanks.
highlights: Three disc sizes: 30, 40 and 50 mm
Clear glass body that disappears against the back glass
Compact shape tucks into an inside corner of the tank
ADA matches sizes to tank length: 30 for 90 cm, 40 for 90 to 120 cm, 50 for 120 to 180 cm
bestFor: Pressurised CO2 tanks of 90 cm and up where you want a neat, nearly invisible diffuser and are happy to clean glass now and then.
watchOut: Glass is fragile, and the disc clogs over time, so expect occasional soaking in diluted bleach.

specs.Material: Glass body with ceramic diffuser disc

name: Pollen Glass Type 3
summary: A classic upright glass CO2 diffuser from ADA, with the ceramic disc set into a glass cup. The Type 3 update turned the tube inlet upright so the CO2 line connects without a tight bend.
highlights: All-glass upright diffuser with ceramic disc
Upright inlet, so the CO2 tube connects without bending
Clear glass keeps it low-key in a scape
bestFor: Small to medium pressurised CO2 tanks where an upright glass diffuser suits the look.
watchOut: Like all glass diffusers it is fragile and needs regular cleaning to keep bubbles fine.

name: PS-SC Speed Controller
summary: A small inline needle valve with push-fit ends for ADA's pressure-resistant CO2 tubing. It lets you fine-tune gas flow on a line, which is handy when one cylinder feeds more than one tank.
highlights: Knurled needle adjuster for fine control
Push-fit connectors for pressure-resistant tube
ADA advises one per line when a CO2 supply is split, and for rates under about 1 bubble per second
bestFor: Keepers running pressurised CO2 who want finer adjustment than their regulator gives, or split lines to two tanks.
watchOut: It is a flow valve, not a full regulator, so you still need a proper pressure regulator on the cylinder.

name: Lily Pipe
summary: ADA's glass inflow and outflow pipes that replace the plastic pipes of a canister filter. The outflow's flared lip spreads water in a gentle wide stream, and the clear glass nearly vanishes in the tank.
highlights: Clear glass for a clean, almost invisible look
Outflow P-4 has a flared mouth for a soft, wide flow
Inflow V-5 has a slotted intake and suction cup mount
Both listed for 13 mm hose
bestFor: Planted tanks with a canister filter where the plumbing is on show and you want it to disappear.
watchOut: Glass breaks easily and shows biofilm quickly, so it needs gentle handling and regular pipe-brush cleaning.

name: Metal Pipe Flow
summary: Stainless steel versions of ADA's inflow and outflow pipes. They keep the slim lily-pipe shape but will not snap if knocked, and the outflow nozzle swivels to aim the flow.
highlights: Stainless steel, far tougher than glass
Outflow P-1 has a rotating nozzle to direct flow
Inflow V-1 has a removable end cap for easier cleaning
Both listed for 13 mm hose
bestFor: Keepers who like the lily-pipe look but have broken glass pipes before, or have kids and pets around the tank.
watchOut: They are not see-through, so they are more visible than glass in a bright tank.

name: Pro Pinsettes
summary: ADA's long, fine-tipped stainless planting tweezers, sold in several lengths. The slim tips grip single stems and small portions of carpet plants without crushing them.
highlights: Several lengths to suit tank depth
Fine straight tips for stems and carpet portions
Stainless steel
bestFor: Planting stem plants and carpets in medium to deep aquascapes.

name: Pinsettes Series M
summary: Straight stainless tweezers with wider, flat grip sections, easier to hold steady for long planting sessions than very thin tweezers.
highlights: Wide flat handle for a steady grip
Fine straight tips
Stainless steel
bestFor: Everyday planting and moving small items in the tank.

name: Pro Scissors Wave
summary: Long stainless scissors with an S-shaped wave that keeps your hand above the water while the blades sit flat against a carpet. The go-to shape for trimming foreground plants.
highlights: Wave-shaped shank for trimming carpets flat
Long reach for standard aquascape depths
Stainless steel
bestFor: Trimming carpets and low plants in medium to large aquascapes.

name: Adapro Scissors Spring
summary: Spring-action scissors that open by themselves after each cut, operated with a squeeze rather than finger loops. That makes lots of small trims less tiring and gives good control in tight spots.
highlights: Spring-loaded, squeeze to cut
Precise for trimming moss and stems in tight spaces
Stainless steel
bestFor: Detailed trimming of moss, stems and small plants, especially if loop scissors make your hand ache.

name: Pro Razor
summary: A long-handled stainless glass scraper with a replaceable razor blade, for taking algae film and spots off the glass. The Mini version is shorter for small tanks.
highlights: Replaceable razor blade holder on a long stainless shaft
Two sizes: Pro Razor and Pro Razor Mini
Slim shaft reaches behind plants and hardscape
bestFor: Keeping the front glass of a glass (not acrylic) planted tank spotless.
watchOut: Never use on acrylic, and keep the blade away from silicone seams.

name: Sand Flattener
summary: A long stainless tool with a flat triangular plate for smoothing and levelling sand or soil, even after the tank is filled. Great for tidying a cosmetic sand path along the front glass.
highlights: Flat triangular plate for levelling sand and soil
Long shaft works in a filled tank
Stainless steel
bestFor: Aquascapes with a sand foreground or path that needs regular smoothing.

name: La Plata Sand
summary: A fine, pale natural sand used for paths, foreground patches and beach areas in nature aquariums. Its light colour brightens the front of a layout and contrasts well with dark aqua soil.
highlights: Fine, pale natural sand
Classic choice for sand paths and open foreground areas
Sold in 2 kg bags
bestFor: Iwagumi and nature aquarium layouts that need a clean, bright foreground or path.
watchOut: Keep it separated from soil with stones or a divider, or the two will mix over time.

name: Colorado Sand
summary: A natural sand with a light sandy-beige tone, a touch warmer than La Plata Sand. It suits paths and foregrounds where you want a more natural, riverbed feel.
highlights: Warm beige natural sand
Good for paths, beaches and open foreground areas
Sold in 2 kg bags
bestFor: Nature-style and riverbank layouts that want a softer, warmer foreground than white sand.
watchOut: Like any cosmetic sand, it will mix into soil unless the two are kept apart.

name: Aqua Gravel
summary: A natural mixed-colour gravel in browns, greys and tans. It works for streambed details, filling gaps around stones or as a coarser foreground accent.
highlights: Natural river gravel in mixed earthy colours
Useful for streambeds and detailing around rock
Sold in 2 kg bags
bestFor: Adding texture and a natural riverbed look to the foreground of a planted tank.
watchOut: Too coarse for carpet plants to root in, so use it as an accent rather than a planting substrate.
